landmarks.name: The Old Town Wall
landmarks.desc: The city's first wall, 400 years old; long stretches pulled down for houses.

landmarks.name: Crownhold
landmarks.desc: The giant royal castle on its crag: two curtain walls, 26 towers and a 50 m keep.

landmarks.name: The Crown Tower
landmarks.desc: 50 m great keep, eight storeys: the throne room is on the fifth.

landmarks.name: The Crowning Stone
landmarks.desc: A prehistoric stone carried up from the river: every monarch is crowned on it.

landmarks.name: The Grand Market
landmarks.desc: Biggest market in the city: cloth, pots, poultry, cheese, everything; the Moot Hill rises in its corner.

landmarks.name: Moot Hill
landmarks.desc: A Bronze Age burial mound left in the Grand Market; the city's assemblies are still held on top.

landmarks.name: The Kingstone
landmarks.desc: A 6 m menhir at the crossroads where the North and West roads meet. Older than any road.

landmarks.name: Wardenhouse - YOUR HOUSE
landmarks.desc: Home of The Warden of the Stones, facing the Kingstone. Start here.

landmarks.name: The Spice Bazaar
landmarks.desc: A 160 m covered street of spice, silk and incense sellers.

landmarks.name: Wool Hall
landmarks.desc: Wool exchange: fleeces from a hundred hill farms are graded and sold.

landmarks.name: Muster Square
landmarks.desc: Parade ground below the castle where the city militia drills.

landmarks.name: Shambles Market
landmarks.desc: The butchers' street-market (bring a strong stomach).

landmarks.name: The Sleeping Giant inn
landmarks.desc: The oldest inn in the city, built against the Old Town wall.

landmarks.name: The Three Kings' Table
landmarks.desc: A portal tomb on the Minster lawn; the island was holy before the Minster was.

landmarks.name: Stonehallow Minster
landmarks.desc: Gothic cathedral on King's Isle; its spire reaches 120 m, the tallest thing in the realm.

landmarks.name: The Grand Bridge
landmarks.desc: Two stone spans across both arms of the river; the north span carries 14 shops.

landmarks.name: The Royal Menagerie
landmarks.desc: Lions, a bear, an elephant from the south and the King's white stags.

landmarks.name: The Giant's Grave
landmarks.desc: A 90 m long barrow kept as a lawn in the palace gardens.

landmarks.name: Palace of the Seven Gardens
landmarks.desc: The royal summer palace and its seven gardens: maze, parterres, orchard, water garden, lime walk, menagerie and the Giant's Grave.

landmarks.name: The Queen's Maze
landmarks.desc: A 66 m hedge maze with a sundial stone at its heart.

landmarks.name: Flower Market
landmarks.desc: Flowers, herbs and songbirds for the palace quarter.

landmarks.name: Grain Exchange
landmarks.desc: Corn factors shout prices under the great timber roof.

landmarks.name: Merchant Palaces
landmarks.desc: Four courtyard palaces of the great trading houses.

landmarks.name: King's Quay
landmarks.desc: Half a kilometre of stone quays, warehouses, treadwheel cranes and cogs from overseas.

landmarks.name: Fish Market
landmarks.desc: Fishwives, oysters and the catch of the morning boats.

landmarks.name: The Ropewalk
landmarks.desc: A shed 300 m long where hemp is twisted into ships' cables.

landmarks.name: Harbour Light
landmarks.desc: Lighthouse at the end of the breakwater guiding cogs into the river mouth.

landmarks.name: The Star Citadel
landmarks.desc: Five-pointed bastioned fortress guarding the river's entry into the city.

landmarks.name: The Arsenal
landmarks.desc: Where the city's crossbows, pikes and siege engines are built and stored.

landmarks.name: Drill Field & Archery Butts
landmarks.desc: Every man of the city must shoot at the butts on Sundays.

landmarks.name: Camp of the Iron Host
landmarks.desc: A standing camp of 2,000 soldiers: tents, horse lines and a palisade.

landmarks.name: Siege Yard
landmarks.desc: Trebuchets and mangonels being built and tested.

landmarks.name: Cavalry Paddocks
landmarks.desc: Grazing and training for the knights' horses.

landmarks.name: Night Market
landmarks.desc: Opens at dusk under lanterns: hot food, music, fortune-tellers.

landmarks.name: The Lantern Playhouse
landmarks.desc: Round wooden playhouse for 1,500: comedies, tragedies and riots.

landmarks.name: Bear Garden
landmarks.desc: Animal-baiting pit and its noisy galleries.

landmarks.name: Bathhouse of the Swan
landmarks.desc: Steam rooms, tubs and gossip.

landmarks.name: Bathhouse of the Mermaid
landmarks.desc: Steam rooms, tubs and gossip.

landmarks.name: The Nine Sisters
landmarks.desc: Nine little stones in a ring, kept inside the pleasure gardens; lovers meet here.

landmarks.name: Lantern Gardens
landmarks.desc: Pleasure gardens lit with a thousand lanterns on summer nights.

landmarks.name: The Great Auditorium
landmarks.desc: Stone amphitheatre seating 8,000 for proclamations, plays and tournaments.

landmarks.name: Cattle Market
landmarks.desc: Pens of cattle, sheep and pigs inside the South Gate.

landmarks.name: Tanners' Reach
landmarks.desc: Downwind and downstream: tanneries, dye vats in three colours, kilns, a bell foundry, glassworks and a brewery.

landmarks.name: The Shipyard
landmarks.desc: Four slipways building war cogs for the crown, with a sail loft and mast pond.

landmarks.name: College of the Seven Stars
landmarks.desc: A college of the university: hall, chapel, library and rooms round a grass court.

landmarks.name: The Druids' Row
landmarks.desc: Eight stones in a dead-straight line; the astronomers say it points at the midwinter sunrise.

landmarks.name: Scholars' Hill University
landmarks.desc: Three colleges, a library, an observatory, an anatomy theatre and the Hall of Disputations.

landmarks.name: Book Market
landmarks.desc: Copyists, maps, almanacs and forbidden books under the counter.

landmarks.name: West Bridge
landmarks.desc: Six arches and two corn mills where the scholars cross into the Westgate.

landmarks.name: St. Bartholomew's Fair Field
landmarks.desc: A fair field the size of the Old Town: tents, pavilions, stages, a jousting tiltyard, archery, a maypole. Busiest in late August.

landmarks.name: Field of Rest
landmarks.desc: The great cemetery beyond the walls.

landmarks.name: Whitecross Abbey
landmarks.desc: Benedictine abbey with its own farms, fishponds and bees.

landmarks.name: Leper House of St. Lazarus
landmarks.desc: Kept far outside the walls, with its own chapel and garden.

landmarks.name: The Old Ring
landmarks.desc: An Iron Age hillfort: three rings of ramparts on the hill; a hermit now lives inside.

landmarks.name: Saltreed Marsh
landmarks.desc: Reedbeds, herons and smugglers' paths.

landmarks.name: Salt Pans
landmarks.desc: Sea water evaporates in shallow pans; salt is the city's white gold.

landmarks.name: South Down windmills
landmarks.desc: Four post-mills grinding the southern harvest.

landmarks.name: Haymarket
landmarks.desc: Carters bring hay, straw and firewood down from the hills.

landmarks.name: Brigid's Well & Stone
landmarks.desc: A holy spring guarded by an ancient standing stone; pilgrims tie ribbons to it.

landmarks.name: Pilgrims' Hospice
landmarks.desc: Free beds and soup for pilgrims arriving from the north.

landmarks.name: Mere Abbey
landmarks.desc: Cistercian abbey on the shore of the Mirror Mere.

landmarks.name: Royal Hunting Lodge
landmarks.desc: The King's lodge deep in the Royal Forest.

landmarks.name: Crownback Vineyards
landmarks.desc: South-facing terraces of vines above the palace.

landmarks.name: Horse Fair
landmarks.desc: Horse dealers' field outside the West Gate.

landmarks.name: Eastfold
landmarks.desc: Fishing village on Gull Bay: huts on stilts, drying racks and boats on the shingle.

landmarks.name: Raven Light
landmarks.desc: Lighthouse on the cliffs of Raven Head.

landmarks.name: The Sea Stones
landmarks.desc: A tiny stone ring and a rock carved with cups and rings, on the windiest cliff in the realm.

landmarks.name: Gull Rock Sea Fort
landmarks.desc: Round fort on an island guarding the river mouth; reached only by boat.

landmarks.name: Lantern Point
landmarks.desc: Smugglers' village and lighthouse on the southern headland.

landmarks.name: Nunnery of St. Clare
landmarks.desc: One of the city's great religious or charitable houses.

landmarks.name: Greyfriars
landmarks.desc: One of the city's great religious or charitable houses.

landmarks.name: Blackfriars
landmarks.desc: One of the city's great religious or charitable houses.

landmarks.name: Hospital of St. Brigid
landmarks.desc: One of the city's great religious or charitable houses.

landmarks.name: Almshouses of the Twelve
landmarks.desc: One of the city's great religious or charitable houses.

landmarks.name: Jail & Court of Pie Powder
landmarks.desc: Locks, chains and a magistrate who can be bribed.

landmarks.desc: Guild hall of one of the city's trades.

landmarks.desc: Guild hall of one of the city's trades.

landmarks.name: Tavern of the Drowned Rat
landmarks.desc: Ale, gossip and trouble.

landmarks.name: The Crooked Cup
landmarks.desc: Ale, gossip and trouble.

landmarks.name: The Golden Goose
landmarks.desc: Ale, gossip and trouble.

landmarks.name: The Mermaid
landmarks.desc: Ale, gossip and trouble.

landmarks.name: The Sleeping Bishop
landmarks.desc: Ale, gossip and trouble.

landmarks.name: Debtors' Prison
landmarks.desc: Locks, chains and a magistrate who can be bribed.

landmarks.name: Alchemist's Tower
landmarks.desc: Smoke of strange colours pours from its windows at night.

landmarks.name: Clockmakers' Hall
landmarks.desc: Guild hall of one of the city's trades.
